written: 2026-11-14, after the F1 results were read, before any code of this addendum ran on real states
why: Control F1 of flip_rule.json expected the FP32 reference token to equal the emitted token as often as exp01's C1 alignment. That was a mis-specification: C1 compares the emitted token with the argmax of the BF16 product, not with the reference. The F1 results measured 99.59% (Qwen3-8B), 99.57% (Gemma 4) and 97.44% (Sarvam-30B) against C1's 1.0000, 99.8% and 98.8%. flip_rule.json is left as hashed. This addendum states the control as it should have been and adds the measurement the mismatch points to.
unchanged: states, reference, rules, noise, outcomes, intervals and the F0 control, all as in flip_rule.json. The results already reported under flip_rule.json are not rerun or changed.
copy_added: bf16_prod: the BF16 product of the BF16 state and the BF16 head, computed as exp01 computes it for C1 ((h.bfloat16() @ Wb.T) on the GPU, read back as FP32), 128 states at a time. It stands for the stock head. No shift.

controls.F1_corrected: on greedy states, the number of states whose bf16_prod argmax equals the emitted token equals the c1_match count exp01 stored for the same states (results/<model>/greedy_*.json), exactly, in every job. Stored totals: 28,940 of 28,940 (Qwen3-8B), 29,581 of 29,641 (Gemma 4); Sarvam-30B's is read from the volume. A mismatch means this product is not exp01's and the bf16_prod numbers are reported as a different BF16 implementation, not as the stock head.
controls.F0: rerun as in flip_rule.json is not needed: bf16_prod has no A3 counterpart. The reference tokens stored here must equal the reference tokens stored by the F1 run on every state and rule (flip/<model>, key ref/<rule>); any difference invalidates this addendum's run.

outcomes.flip: per state and rule: cert_core.decide on the bf16_prod logits (soft-cap applied in FP32, same noise) differs from the reference token
outcomes.tie: greedy: the two largest bf16_prod logits are equal

primary_outcome: greedy flip rate of bf16_prod against the reference, each model, with the 95% prompt-bootstrap interval, set beside the INT8 and first-pass-alone rates of F1
known_weaknesses: The BF16 product depends on the BLAS path (batch shape, library version); this is the analysis image's, as in exp01's C1, not the generating run's. On Sarvam-30B the generating run used another torch version, which is why C1 is 98.8% there. Gemma 4's stock head applies the soft-cap in BF16; here it is applied in FP32 to the BF16 logits. Written after seeing F1's results, including the 118 Qwen3-8B states where the reference differs from the emitted token.

prediction_written_before_running.qwen3_8b: F1_corrected holds, and since every emitted token is the bf16_prod argmax, exactly 118 of 28,940 greedy states flip (0.41%)
prediction_written_before_running.sarvam_30b: greedy flip rate between 1.5% and 3.5%, higher than INT8's 1.18%
prediction_written_before_running.gaps: median gap on flipped greedy states below 0.15 logits on every model (rounding-level), and more than a third of greedy flips are exact ties in the BF16 logits
prediction_written_before_running.vs_int8: bf16_prod flips more often than INT8 on greedy, on every model
